In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for ranking from multi-wise comparison, the winner feedback setting is more efficient than the full-ranking feedback one and the sample complexity for ranking from multi-wised comparisons is always smaller than that for ranking from pairwise comparisons.

, in terms of the sample complexity, utilizing multi-wise comparisons does not help reduce the sample complexity of ranking from the winner feedback, while it does help reduce the sample com- plexity of ranking from the full-ranking feedback.

, under the full ranking feedback setting, the sample complexity for ranking from multi-wise comparison is always at least as large as that for ranking from pairwise comparisons and, under the winner ranking feedback setting, ranking from $m$-wise comparisons can reduce the number of comparisons required for ranking up to an order of $m$ factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduction of sample complexity is not trivial for the ranking problems from multi-wise comparisons and the reduction is more significant for top-$k$, compared to full ranking.

, in the winner feedback case, the sample complexity of ranking with multi-wise comparisons is no more than that of ranking from pairwise comparisons, while in the full-ranking feedback case, the former can be much smaller than the latter.
, in the fundamental setting, utilizing multi-wise comparisons cannot reduce the sample complexity of the ranking problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the winner feedback is available, one can reduce sample complexity up to an $O(\log{m})$ factor compared to ranking from $m$ pairwise comparisons.
, when the feedback is the winner or the full ranking, multi-wise comparisons can significantly reduce the sample complexity of the ranking problems.
the sample complexity bounds for the ranking problem under the multi-wise comparison model are very different from those under the pairwise comparison model.
